mainTopic: How long time-limited vows last (today, one day, week, month, year, and plain "a day"), and רבי נתן's view that vows are better undone
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of vows that are limited in time. אביי challenges רב יוסף's גזירה on a vow of "היום" (today): if we worry about mix-ups, why not also make a decree about "יום אחד" (one day)? רב יוסף answers that the mix-up only goes in one direction. רבינא then reports a different explanation: רב ירמיה בר אבא's ruling follows רבי נתן, who teaches that making a נדר is like building a private altar, so it is better to have a חכם undo it. Next the גמרא explains the משנה's rulings on "this week" and "this month". A week vow includes the day of שבת. In a month vow, even the first day of a two-day ראש חודש counts with the new month, because people call it ראש חודש. After quoting the rule for "this year", the גמרא asks whether a vow for plain "יום" (a day) means "today" or a full twenty-four hours. A proof from our משנה fails because its two halves point in opposite directions. רב אשי then brings a new proof from a "this year" vow in a leap year, and the גמרא's working out of that case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי asks why there is no matching decree for a one-day vow
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: if we make a גזירה on a "היום" vow because of "יום אחד", we should also make a גזירה on "יום אחד" because of "היום".
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If so, we should also make a decree about a vow of "one day" because of a vow of "today"!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's earlier reason for the extra strictness on a vow of "היום". He argues that the same worry should cause a decree in the other direction too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף explained that we are strict on a "היום" vow because people might confuse it with a "יום אחד" vow. אביי asks: confusion can go both ways. A "יום אחד" vow lasts a full 24 hours, so it might end in the middle of a day, and people might then think a "היום" vow also ends mid-day. So why not also add strictness to the "יום אחד" vow?

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reasoning is right
Let them make a decree (גזירה); a protective rule from the חכמים
"One day": a vow lasting a full 24 hours
"Today": a vow lasting until this day ends at nightfall

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: This is אביי speaking to רב יוסף.

phrases.english: let them make a decree about "one day"
because of "today"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's reason for the גזירה, which came just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's explanation that a "היום" vow gets extra strictness because of "יום אחד".
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the worry is confusion between the two vows, the confusion should work both ways, so a matching decree should exist for "יום אחד".

steps.title: The mix-up only goes one way
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that people might confuse "היום" with "יום אחד", but they would not confuse "יום אחד" with "היום".
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: "Today" can be mixed up with "one day", but "one day" is not mixed up with "today".
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his גזירה by saying the confusion only happens in one direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone with a "היום" vow might think it works like "יום אחד", so a protective rule is needed there. But someone who hears about a "יום אחד" vow ending mid-day will not think a "היום" vow also ends mid-day, because "today" plainly means until the day is over. A גזירה is only made where a real mistake is likely.

keyTerms.meaning: Gets mixed up; confused with
Is not mixed up

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה is only made where people are actually likely to make the mistake. A mix-up that only works in one direction only calls for a decree in that direction.

phrases.english: He said to him: "Today" gets mixed up with "one day",
but "one day" does not get mixed up with "today".

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the confusion only works in one direction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the two vows can be confused, both should get a protective decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only "היום" could be mistaken for "יום אחד", so only the "היום" vow needs the decree.

steps.title: רב ירמיה בר אבא's ruling follows רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports, through מרימר and in the name of רב יוסף, that רב ירמיה בר אבא's ruling follows רבי נתן, who says that making a נדר is like building a private altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: מרימר told me that your father said this in the name of רב יוסף: Whose view does רב ירמיה בר אבא's ruling follow? It follows רבי נתן. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי נתן says, anyone who makes a vow is like someone who built a private altar, and one who keeps the vow is like someone who burns offerings on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different explanation of רב ירמיה בר אבא's earlier ruling. Instead of a decree against confusion, the reason is that a person should not stay bound by a נדר at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן compares a נדר to a במה, a private altar that is forbidden. Keeping the vow is like offering on that altar, which makes things worse. So even after the vow's time is up, it is better to go to a חכם and have the vow undone, as if it was never made.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with whose view does it go?
His ruling or teaching
As a ברייתא teaches
A private altar, forbidden once the בית המקדש is the only place for offerings
Burns an offering on an altar

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נתן, making a נדר is like building a forbidden במה, and keeping it is like offering on it. So it is better to have a חכם undo a vow than to keep it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the חז״ל attitude that making vows is discouraged. It also gives a second reason for being strict with a "היום" vow, apart from רב יוסף's גזירה.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Mareimar said to me,
this is what your father said in the name of Rav Yosef:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording; some versions don't have the name יוסף here.

phrases.english: In line with whose view does the ruling go
of Rav Yirmeya bar Abba?
It follows Rabbi Natan.
As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Natan says:
Anyone who makes a vow is as if he built a private altar,
and one who keeps it is as if he burns offerings on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא שְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different basis for רב ירמיה בר אבא's ruling than the גזירה discussed in steps 1-2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ירמיה בר אבא's ruling follows רבי נתן: a נדר is like building a במה, so one should ask a חכם to undo it even after keeping it.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say a "this week" vow covers the whole week?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a vow of "שבת זו" forbids for the entire week, and asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: "This week": he is forbidden for the entire week. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, a vow for "this week". It asks why the משנה bothered to state something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone vows for "this week", it seems clear that the vow lasts for the rest of the week. The גמרא assumes the משנה would not teach something without a reason, so it asks what the משנה is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: "This week"; here שבת means the week
All of it; the whole
It's obvious! Why say it?

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word שבת means "week", not only the seventh day. The question in the next step is whether the day of שבת itself is included in "this week".

phrases.english: "This week": he is forbidden
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about a vow for "this week".

phrases.english: for the entire week.
That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a "שבת זו" vow lasts the whole week.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems self-evident, so why does the משנה need to teach it?

steps.title: The vow includes שבת itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought he meant only the weekdays, so the משנה teaches that the day of שבת is included too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said he meant only the days of the week. So the משנה teaches us that it includes the whole week.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what new point the משנה is teaching about a "this week" vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the משנה, we might think "this week" means only the weekdays and leaves out שבת itself. The משנה teaches that the vow covers the full week, including the day of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said; what you might have thought
The days of the week; the weekdays
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: A vow for "שבת זו" (this week) lasts the whole week, including the day of שבת, not only the weekdays.

phrases.english: You might have said:
he meant the days of the week,
phrases.notes: Meaning just the weekdays, leaving out the day of שבת itself.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the possible mistake the משנה prevents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "This week" might mean only the weekdays, leaving out שבת itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow covers the whole week, including שבת.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say that ראש חודש belongs to the coming month?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a vow of "this month" forbids for the whole month, with ראש חודש counted as part of the next month. It asks why this needs to be said at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if someone vows "this month," it is forbidden the whole month, and ראש חודש counts as part of the coming month. Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a vow of "this month." It complains that the line seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the question about "שבת זו" in step 4. ראש חודש is the first day of the new month, so of course it is not part of the old month. The גמרא wants to know what new thing the משנה is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: "This month": a vow limited to the current month
The New Moon, the start of a new month
Belongs to the coming month (the future)
"It's obvious!": a challenge asking why something needs to be said

phrases.english: If he vows "this month," it is forbidden for the whole month,
and ראש חודש counts as part of the coming month.
This is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 4, now aimed at the next case in the משנה (a month instead of a week).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that ראש חודש belongs to the coming month
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ראש חודש is clearly the start of the new month, so saying so seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The case where ראש חודש lasts two days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a חודש חסר, when ראש חודש lasts two days. Even the first of those days, which is really the old month's last day, counts with the new month, because people call it ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה was needed for a חודש חסר. You might have thought that the first day of ראש חודש belongs to the past month, so the vow would end with that day and he would not be forbidden afterward. So it teaches us that people call it "the head of the month," which means it belongs to the new month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the "it's obvious" question. It shows a tricky case where the משנה's rule really does teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes ראש חודש is two days, and the first day is really the thirtieth day of the old month. Someone might think that day belongs to the old month. The משנה teaches that it follows how people speak: they call it ראש חודש of the new month, so it counts with the new month.

keyTerms.meaning: A "deficient month": the גמרא's name for the case where ראש חודש lasts two days
Belongs to the past month
"You might have said": introduces a mistaken first thought
"It teaches us": introduces the actual lesson
"Head of the month": the everyday Aramaic name for ראש חודש

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether ראש חודש is part of the new month in general. It is only about the first day of a two-day ראש חודש, which is really the last day of the old month.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows again that vows follow how people normally speak, not the exact calendar count.

phrases.english: It was needed for a deficient month,
phrases.notes: This is the case where ראש חודש is two days, and he made the vow on the first of them.

phrases.english: you might have said:
that ראש חודש belongs to the past month,
and so he should not be forbidden afterward,
so it teaches us
people call it "the head of the month."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא question of step 6 by pointing to a case that is not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a specific, less obvious case (a two-day ראש חודש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first day of a two-day ראש חודש is really part of the old month, so the vow would end with it and he would not be forbidden afterward.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since people call that day ראש חודש, it counts with the new month.

steps.title: A vow of "this year"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that a vow of "this year" forbids for the whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone vows "this year," it is forbidden for the entire year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא simply quotes the next line of the משנה, about a vow for "this year," and adds no question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as "this week" and "this month." The vow lasts until the current year ends, and the גמרא raises no challenge here.

keyTerms.meaning: "This year": a vow limited to the current year
All of it, the entire

phrases.english: If he vows "this year,"
it is forbidden for the entire year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה after the month case is settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of "this year" lasts until the end of the current year.

steps.title: Does a vow for "a day" mean "today" or a full day?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask: if someone vows not to taste wine for "a day," is it like saying "today" (until nightfall) or like "one day" (a full twenty-four hours)?
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars asked: if he said, "Wine is קונם, that I will not taste it for a day," what is the law? Is it like "today," or like "one day"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about unclear wording in a vow. It is setting up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא explained that "היום" ends at nightfall, while "יום אחד" lasts a full twenty-four hours. Now someone just said "יום," without either word added. The question is which of the two he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was asked of them": introduces a real question the scholars were unsure about
A word used to make something forbidden by vow, like a קרבן
Taste
"What is his law?"

phrases.english: The scholars asked:
if he said, "Wine is קונם, that I will not taste it for a day,"
what is the law for him?
Is it like "today," or like "one day"?
phrases.notes: "Today" ends at nightfall, and "one day" lasts a full twenty-four hours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that builds on the earlier difference between "היום" and "יום אחד" from steps 1 and 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vow for "יום" alone ends at nightfall, like "היום," or lasts twenty-four hours, like "יום אחד."

steps.title: A proof from the first part of the משנה: "today" lasts until dark
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a vow of "today" lasts only until nightfall. The גמרא reads this as implying that a plain "a day" would last a full 24 hours, like "one day."
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from our משנה: "Wine is קונם, so I will not taste it today." He is forbidden only until it gets dark. This implies that "a day" is like "one day."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question about "a day" by looking closely at the wording of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits the vow to nightfall only when he said "today." The גמרא reasons that if a plain "a day" also meant until dark, the משנה would not need the word "today." So it concludes that "a day" must mean a full 24 hours.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as proof
A word used to make a vow that forbids something
Until it gets dark, meaning the end of the day
One day, meaning a full 24 hours

phrases.english: Come and hear from our משנה:
"Wine is konam, so I will not taste it today"
phrases.notes: Saying קונם makes the wine forbidden to him, the way a vow does.

phrases.english: he is forbidden only until it gets dark.
This implies that "a day" is like "one day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question raised in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a vow of "a day" lasts a full 24 hours, like "one day."
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first part of the משנה: a vow of "today" lasts only until dark, which implies plain "a day" is longer.

steps.title: The last part of the משנה points the other way, so no proof
steps.stepSummary: The last part of the משנה says "one day" lasts 24 hours. That implies plain "a day" is like "today." Since the two parts imply opposite things, nothing can be learned from this משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the end of the משנה: if he said "one day," he is forbidden from one day to the same time the next day. This implies that "a day" is like "today." So nothing can be learned from this משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by reading the end of the same משנה, which implies the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If plain "a day" already meant 24 hours, the משנה would not need to say "one day" to get 24 hours. So the end of the משנה suggests "a day" means only until dark. Each part of the משנה can be read to imply opposite things, so the משנה does not settle the question either way.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of a משנה or ברייתא
From day to day: from now until the same time tomorrow
Nothing can be learned from it

steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not fail because the משנה is wrong. It fails because "a day" falls between the two cases the משנה lists, so you cannot tell which case it belongs with.

phrases.english: Say the end part of the משנה:
if he said "one day"
he is forbidden from one day to the next day.
This implies that "a day" is like "today."
Rather, nothing can be learned from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 10 using the end of the same משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof from this משנה. The question from step 9 still needs an answer, so רב אשי offers a new proof in step 12.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The end of the משנה implies the opposite of the beginning, so neither implication can be relied on.

steps.title: רב אשי brings a new proof from a vow for "this year"
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes the משנה that if someone vows off wine for "this year" and the year becomes a leap year, he is forbidden for the extra month too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Come and hear: "Wine is קונם, so I will not taste it this year." If the year was made a leap year, he is forbidden during the year and during its extra month.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tries a different source to answer the question about "a day."
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה is about a vow for a year, not a day, but רב אשי thinks it can teach how such vows are read. The vow covers the whole calendar year, even when an extra month is added. The גמרא will now work out the exact case to see if it really helps.

keyTerms.meaning: A leading אמורא in בבל who brings this proof
The year was made a leap year
The extra month added in a leap year

phrases.english: רב אשי said: Come and hear:
"Wine is konam, so I will not taste it this year"
if the year was made a leap year,
he is forbidden during it and during its extra month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new proof is offered from a different משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The open question of step 9: whether "a day" means "today" or "one day."
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a vow for "this year" that becomes a leap year.

steps.title: What exact case is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the exact situation of the "this year" vow is, to see how it helps.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks what exact case the משנה means, to prepare for the answer on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the משנה can answer the question about "a day," the גמרא has to pin down the exact wording and situation it is talking about. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what exact case the משנה quoted in step 12 is talking about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case and wording of the "this year" vow, so the גמרא can see whether it answers the question about "a day."
